newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE RADUCIOIU INSPIRES WEST HAM COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUBSTITUTE RADUCIOIU INSPIRES WEST HAM COMEBACK.

text.p: Romanian substitute Florin Raducioiu fired a West Ham comeback in which they hit two late goals in two minutes to snatch a 2-2 draw against champions Manchester United in the English premier league on Sunday.

United were leading through goals from Norwegian Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and England midfielder David Beckham with only 13 minutes left when home side West Ham suddenly transformed the shape of the game.
First, Raducioiu shrugged aside Norwegian defender Ronnie Johnsen to create the room he needed to drive his first league goal past Denmark's Peter Schmeichel in the 78th minute.
Two minutes later, Romanian Ilie Dumitrescu played into the box, Michael Hughes gathered the ball and when he attempted to round Schmeichel the goalkeeper brought him crashing to the ground.
The referee had no doubts it was a penalty and defender Julian Dicks' finish -- his fourth successful spot-kick of the season -- was equally emphatic, a thunderous left-footer past Schmeichel.
United, having been given the run-around before halftime, seized the initiative through two moments of creative genius by skipper Eric Cantona.
The Frenchman produced a pass of outstanding vision with the outside of his right foot to allow Solskjaer to grab his first away goal in the 54th minute.
Then Cantona started the move that ended with Beckham chipping into the top corner to make it 2-0 after 75 minutes.
However, the Raducioiu-inspired fightback earned West Ham a worthy point and left United in sixth place, eight points behind leaders Arsenal.
